title: Applied ML weekly standup — Ember model onboarding & sparse-KV experiments
content:
Weekly capture: May 20 2026 — Standup + research notes (informal).

Attendees: Priya (scribe), Evan, Sofia, Liam, Hanna, optional: Marco (ops).
Context: Rapid onboarding for a new open model we’re evaluating for compact-hosting, internal name Ember-3.5B (decoder-only, 3.5B weights, roughly similar to community 3.3–3.7B variants). Primary workstreams this week: (A) quantization strategy (bit-slice + selective-embedding), (B) sparse-KV prefetch experiments to reduce cold-step latency, (C) eval runner integration and regression checks for instruction-following, (D) small-scale rollout plan to Dedicated pools.

1) Quick summary / decisions
- Decision: proceed with a two-track quantization approach for Ember: 6-bit baseline (symmetric) for fast iteration, and a targeted 4-bit pipeline (bit-slice + outlier handling) for the best cost win.
- Decision: enable sparse-KV prefetch as an opt-in runtime flag for Ember testing only; default off for hosted.
- We will gate any 4-bit rollout on passing the local eval suite + A/B quality threshold (max 3% drop in instr-follow f1 relative to fp16 baseline).

2) Wins / progress
- Data prep: tokenizer checks complete; no unexpected OOV tokens for our evaluation prompts.
- First-pass 6-bit symmetric quant for Ember converged without NaNs; average inference memory reduced ~34%.
- Sparse-KV prefetch prototype implemented by Liam — when prefetch hits, P50 step latency reduced ~18% on short-context traces (<=128 tokens).
- Eval harness: Sofia wired Ember into the eval runner; initial instruction-following suite produced baseline metrics (fp16) that look reasonable.

3) Signals & numbers (early, noisy)
- Baseline (fp16) Ember-3.5B single-token generation on testbox (A100, batch=1): P50 28ms, P95 62ms, throughput ~36 tok/s steady-state.
- 6-bit symmetric quant: P50 31ms (+3ms), P95 70ms (+8ms), throughput ~44 tok/s (due to memory fit enabling larger microbatching).
- 4-bit bit-slice (early impl, no outlier handling yet): instability observed for very long-context rolls >1024 steps; mean perplexity on wiki-dev went up by ~6% (needs calibration).
- Sparse-KV prefetch: on short-context chat traces, token latency P50 dropped from 28ms -> 23ms when prefetch hit; hit-rate depends on session locality (currently ~37% in synthetic replay).
- Eval: instruction-following (IF) micro-eval: fp16 baseline IF-F1 = 0.78, 6-bit IF-F1 = 0.76 (drop ~2.6%), 4-bit uncalibrated IF-F1 = 0.71 (drop ~8.9%).

4) Current blockers / open risks
- 4-bit reliability: outlier activation handling not integrated yet — leads to hallucination spikes in some prompts. Need a deterministic fallback path (detect high-variance logits -> re-run on 6-bit or fp16).
- Sparse-KV variance: prefetch helps short traces but increases tail latency on certain mixed workloads due to extra buffer copying in the runtime. Need microbenchmark with mixed trace distributions.
- Eval coverage: existing instruction-following set misses certain dialog-turn continuity checks (we observed failures that the current metric doesn’t capture). Add continuity-specific tests.

5) Experiments planned next sprint (concurrent)
- Experiment E1: 6-bit + selective 8-bit embedding (embeddings kept at 8-bit) vs full 6-bit. Goal: recover any instruction-follow loss while keeping memory savings. Owner: Evan. Timeline: data-run by 2026-05-26.
- Experiment E2: 4-bit + outlier detection (approximate EMAD threshold) + fallback re-run to 6-bit for flagged tokens. Owner: Sofia. Timeline: prototype by 2026-05-28.
- Experiment E3: Sparse-KV prefetch tuning: compare copy-then-prefetch vs zero-copy prefetch path (runtime patch). Owner: Liam + Marco (ops). Timeline: benchmarks 2026-05-25.
- Experiment E4: Microbatch tuning: combination of automatic microbatch selection + dynamic KV cache sizing to exploit memory reductions from 6-bit. Owner: Hanna. Timeline: 2026-05-27.

6) Eval / quality plan and acceptance criteria
- Must pass unit eval battery: no MTURK-like regressions >3% on IF-F1 and no catastrophic token-level divergence on safety triggers.
- Add continuity metric: dialog-turn coherence (new test) — threshold: delta <=2% versus fp16.
- For 4-bit to be considered for Dedicated rollout, must demonstrate median-case parity within 5% IF-F1 and stable tail (P95 token-level divergence) within 10% of fp16.

7) Operational / rollout notes
- Canary strategy: start with dedicated small pool (4xA100 equiv) with ember-6bit as canary; route 5% of dedicated traffic (internal) for 72 hours, collect production eval hooks.
- Logging: enable token-diff logging (hashed) and eval hook sampling at 1/500 requests for quality telemetry in canary.
- Docs: draft shortplaybook for manual rollback if divergence spikes >10% within 1h window. Owner: Priya.

8) Action items (owner + due date)
- Priya: publish quick onboarding playbook + canary checklist (2026-05-24).
- Evan: run E1 and push result summary to the channel (2026-05-26).
- Sofia: prototype E2 with deterministic fallback and run local evals (2026-05-28).
- Liam/Marco: complete zero-copy prefetch microbenchmark and report perf table (2026-05-25).
- Hanna: add dialog continuity tests to eval runner and re-run full suite on 6-bit (2026-05-26).

9) Notes to self / rough ideas (brainstorm)
- Consider hybrid KV index: keep an LRU mini-index in high-bandwidth memory for the last N sessions to raise prefetch hit-rate for active users.
- Evaluate quant-stochastic rounding for dot-product accumulation to see if we can reduce perplexity bump in 4-bit runs.
- Could use a quick light-weight verifier: run a short perplexity check (50 tokens) under fp16 when fallback conditions trigger and abort if delta > X. Cheap safety net.

10) Meeting parking lot / future topics
- Cost modeling: estimate real token-cost improvement for 6bit vs 4bit when accounting for fallback re-runs. (Finance + infra input needed).
- Long-context stability: schedule a focused spike to test >2048 token rolls.

Appendix: quick links / logs- Local perf logs folder: //infrastore/bench/ember/may20 (internal)- Experiment run ids: run-ember-6bit-0520-01, run-ember-4bit-0520-alpha

End of capture — small, actionable set for this week. Will follow up in standup next Wed to surface progress on E2/E3 and the canary checklist.
